role: AK_TEXT (lines and table rows); MODERN_EDITORIAL (the editor's numbers, brackets, note marks and folio references; his footnotes not reproduced)
comment: Frame 033, printed p. 27: the cities of the fifth clime continued, entries 385-400: Qūmis, Ṭamīs near the sea, Astarābādh, Jurjān near the sea, Nīsābūr, Ṭūs, Sarakhs, Marw, Marw al-Rūdh, Ammūya, Bukhārā, Balkh, Samarqand, Ushrūsana, Khujanda and Banākath. Four lines of the editor's footnotes, the last holding one word.

variants: L03: the manuscript reads استاراٮار, with a final ر for the ذ and without the dot of the ب.
L05: the manuscript reads ٮسابور, with a single tooth without a dot before the س; at entries (813-814) the name is written نساٮور, without the ي and without the dot of the ب.
L09: the manuscript reads مرواروذ, as one word; at entry (1975) the name is written مروارود.
L14: the manuscript reads اسروسنه, without the dots of the ش and with a final ه, here and at entry (2207).
L15: the manuscript reads ححنده, without the dots of the خ and the ج and with a final ه; at entry (2207) the name is written خحنده, without the dot of the ج.
observations: The table goes on from frame 032 without a heading: the cities of the fifth clime, entries 385-400. No entry has the word «مدينة». Entries 386 and 387 have no number of Suhrāb; the others have [٣٦٥] (entry 385) and [٣٣٩]-[٣٥١] (entries 388-400).
Signs in the names, transcribed as printed: L10: «امّويه», with a shadda over the م.

L10: to the left of the note mark d stand a small curved stroke like an apostrophe, 6 by 8 px, and a round blot, 13 by 13 px, at the height of the note mark. Neither has the form of the editor's asterisk, a six-pointed star (frame 029, L08), and the notes do not mention them; not transcribed.

Letters printed without their dots in the numerals, transcribed so: the loop of ف or ق without dots in the degrees of the longitude, ڡ (L04), the isolated letter, a loop on a long flat bowl, 80, where L05 prints the same letter with its dot, ف; ڡح (L07, L12), ڡه (L09), ڡر (L11) and ڡط (L13); صٮ (L15), the ص and a final ب without its dot, 92. With their dots: ف (L05), فد (L08), فه (L10); قب (L06), the two dots of the ق above and the dot of the ب below; ن (L03, L06, the minutes of the longitude; L04, L09, L11, the minutes of the latitude); يه (L01); the ز of لز (L05, L06, L15).

L11: the degrees of the longitude, ڡر: the loop without dots joined to a ر; in these numerals the editor reads ر as ز, 7 (introduction, frame 196, p. XVII); transcribed ر as printed. A speck, 5 by 5 px, stands some 45 px to the left of the loop, at the height of its top and away from the head of the ر, above which the dot of a ز would stand; it is not transcribed.
The degrees printed with a final ح, عح (L01, L02), ڡح (L07, L12) and لح (L02-L04, L07-L09, L12), show no dot in the bowl; the same form is a ج without its dot, 3. Transcribed as printed.

L16: the degrees of the latitude, لج: a round dot, 6 by 6 px and as dark as the letters, stands in the bowl below the head of the ج, where this font sets the dot of the letter; it is smaller than the dot of the ج on frames 030 (L14) and 032 (L10), 8 to 9 px across. Transcribed لج, 33; the latitudes of the other entries of the page are 36 to 38 degrees.

L06: the degrees of the longitude, قب, 102, are printed with the two dots of the ق and the dot of the ب; the longitudes of the other entries of the page are 78 to 94 degrees. Transcribed as printed; the editor has no note on the entry.
The isolated ك, 20, is printed with the small inner stroke of the letter (L07, L08, L11, the minutes of the longitude).

Specks, not transcribed: L02, a speck to the right of the ع of the degrees of the longitude; L05, a speck, 4 by 4 px, to the right of the dot of the ف of the degrees of the longitude and lower than it, where the dot is 9 by 10 px; L06, a short horizontal stroke at the foot of the zero of the running number, between the zero and the bracket beside it; L07, two small dark specks to the right of the zero sign of the minutes of the latitude; L09, a dark speck below the line between the minutes and the degrees of the longitude; L13, a short dash to the left of the ل of the minutes of the longitude; L16, a short dash to the right of the ل of the degrees of the latitude.

L10, L11, L13, the degrees of the latitude: «لر»: the letter joined to the foot of the ل has the small pointed head of the joined ر, which stands out 6 to 7 px from the stem, as the ز of «لز» with its dot (L05, L06, L15, 7 to 8 px), where the و of «لو» (L01, L14) is a round loop that stands out 12 to 13 px and begins higher on the stem; in these numerals the editor reads ر as ز, 7 (introduction, frame 196, p. XVII); transcribed ر as printed, which read with ز gives 37.
The page number «— ٢٧ —» stands at the foot, centred.
copy_matter: A faint wavy grey hairline lies in the space between the number of Suhrāb and the running number of entry 388 (L04), a fibre on the paper.
